/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for item in p.iterdir():
 if item.is_file() and item.name.startswith('page-') and item.suffix in {'.txt','.png'}:
  item.unlink()
p.rmdir()
p.parent.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: The calibrated contribution supports weak acceptance. Generating virtual correspondences from triangle means provides an original, simple approximation for a difficult multiview geometry problem, while reusing established 5-point and P3P solvers. Its value lies in practical robust estimation rather than exact algebraic recovery.

Table 2 demonstrates useful accuracy–runtime trade-offs. On PhotoTourism, M+R+F achieves AUC@10 of 69.06 versus HC's 66.63 while reducing RANSAC runtime from 76.45 to 30.54 ms. M±δ+R+F nearly matches 5pt+P3P accuracy (70.47 versus 70.54) at lower runtime (75.78 versus 105.50 ms).

The evaluation is substantial: 5,000 triplets per scene across PhotoTourism and Cambridge Landmarks, two RANSAC frameworks, fixed-iteration runtime comparisons, noise and outlier experiments, and refinement/filtering ablations. Parameters are selected on a held-out scene, and supplementary evaluation using errors across all three camera pairs supports the main calibrated findings.
weaknesses: The shared-focal-length extension has a substantially weaker practical case. In Table 3, 4p3vf(M) achieves AUC@10 of 49.88 at 12.67 ms versus 56.79 at 11.72 ms for 6pt+P3P. The most accurate proposed variant reaches 53.56 at 259.63 ms. Four-match sampling can still be valuable, but its advantage is not demonstrated through a corresponding low-inlier-ratio study, and focal-length estimation errors are not reported.

The approximation's operating conditions remain insufficiently characterized. The triangle-based epipolar-error bound can be large and does not control pose conditioning or convergence of refinement. Aggregate barycentric experiments support the mean heuristic, but do not quantify how its reliability changes with depth variation, viewpoint, or overlap. The acknowledged small-overlap failures therefore remain difficult to predict.

Learning adds little demonstrated benefit after refinement: on PhotoTourism, L+R achieves AUC@10 of 69.88 versus 69.90 for M+R, with runtimes of 297.88 versus 74.94 ms. Additionally, Eq. (2) specifies a signed residual rather than a nonnegative Sampson loss; minimizing it directly need not encourage epipolar consistency. This may be a notation error, but the actual training objective is unclear.

Reproducibility is incomplete. Code is only promised, numerical RANSAC inlier thresholds are not specified, and the precise pose/scale parameterization for LM refinement is omitted. These details matter because refinement and filtering account for much of the practical improvement.

Reporting inconsistencies require clarification. Table 9 gives identical accuracy entries and nearly identical runtimes for corresponding M±δ and L±δ variants despite their different solver costs in Table 10. Separately, the main-text claim that the N-based oracle performs worse conflicts with Table 7 and the supplementary explanation. The latter is a correctable presentation issue; the former leaves uncertainty about the auxiliary learning comparisons.
